label: lf-lean-fire
topic: Can Lean elimination certificates on 1-D heat laws help design bio-based fire-retardant coatings and cut physical fire tests?
summary: Yes, narrowly. Seven simple laws (series resistance and back-face bound, char as added resistance, thermal penetration depth, lumped transient, thin/thick ignition time with critical flux, energy-balance bound on peak HRR) were proved in one Lean file with 16 theorems, all using only the three standard axioms; check.sh passed (0 errors, 0 sorryAx) and a negative control failed as required. Each certificate eliminates a candidate whose best case, inside a declared envelope of thickness, conductivity, thermal inertia and time constant, already breaks a stated limit. It can never approve one: real regulation tests also measure flaming, smoke, flame spread and delamination, which these laws do not model. The registry (upstream/leanbio) has no heat-conduction law, only a diffusive time scale h^2/D and a note that Fick is used as a definition. The saving in tests depends on how many candidates fail on one thermal criterion alone, which is unknown until material data exist; the main risk is a wrong envelope or lumped time constant, which cheap property measurements (not fire tests) can settle.
lay_summary: A fire test asks, among other things, whether the back of a coated board gets too hot too fast.
Simple physics can sometimes say in advance that a coating is too thin or too conductive to ever pass that one question.
We wrote that physics in Lean, a proof checker, so the claim that a candidate cannot pass is checked by machine.
This only works as a way to skip hopeless candidates; it never says a coating is safe.
Fire, smoke, flame spread and peeling are not covered, so every survivor still needs a real test.

findings.claim: Series thermal resistance: layer resistance is thickness/(k A) and series resistances add.
findings.evidence_quote: When resistances are in series, the total resistance is the sum of the resistances
findings.confidence: high (standard law; textbooks Quintiere/Drysdale cited by DOI but not opened)

findings.claim: Proved in Lean: the steady back-face rise DT*Ra/(d/k+Rs+Ra) is at most DT, falls with thickness, and has a lower bound from dmax and kmin; a candidate whose best case exceeds the limit is eliminated (steady state only).
findings.confidence: high for the algebra; the 1-D constant-k model is an assumption

findings.claim: Steady state is an upper bound on a finite-time heating, so a steady bound alone cannot eliminate at a finite test time. A one-node response with time constant at most tau_max is stated as a hypothesis and used.
findings.confidence: high for the proof; medium for physical validity (no PDE comparison theorem was proved)

findings.claim: A char layer as an added series resistance can only lower the steady rise; elimination with envelope on char thickness and conductivity is proved.
findings.evidence_quote: a thermal conductivity model for the fully expanded intumescent coating char, which was assumed to depend on the expansion thickness and the bubble size and distribution (Crossref abstract)
findings.confidence: high for algebra; real char conductivity depends on temperature and morphology so kc_min must be justified

findings.claim: A slab is thermally thick while the penetration depth c*sqrt(alpha t) <= d, equivalently t <= d^2/(c^2 alpha), for any convention constant c>0.

Thin solid with surface loss h never ignites below the critical flux h(Tig-T0) and reaches Tig above it at an explicit time; thick and thin ignition times give elimination given upper bounds on thermal inertia or heat capacity.
findings.source: SFPE Engineering Guide: Piloted Ignition of Solid Materials Under Radiant Exposure (https://www.globalspec.com/reference/76862/203279/thermally-thick, search snippet only); Mikkola and Wichman 1989, 10.1002/fam.810140303 (Crossref-verified, not opened)
findings.evidence_quote: An approximate solution to the time to ignition is derived using the first term of the series expansion and substituting the ignition temperature for the surface temperature. (search snippet)
findings.confidence: medium: t=(pi/4) k rho c (Tig-T0)^2/q^2 is the standard first-term form but I did not read it in a fetched text; the Lean statement is conditional on that definition

findings.claim: Energy balance gives a lower bound on peak HRR: if all fuel burns in n windows of dt, peak >= E/(n dt) >= chi_min m_min dH_min/(n dt). Energy alone gives no upper bound on peak HRR.
findings.confidence: high for the proof; the all-fuel-in-window assumption is strong

findings.claim: Registry check: upstream/leanbio has no heat-conduction, thermal-resistance, ignition or HRR law. Near misses: diffusiveTime h^2/D and diffusiveRate (ThompsonLaws/Hygromorphs.lean), Turing no_instability_of_equal_diffusivity, a Q10 thermal performance curve (Delphi/Perturb.lean), Fick used as a definition (docs/physlib-overlap.md). All seven laws in the table are new to it.

findings.evidence_quote: Fick | Not a theorem. ... Nothing. No diffusion law and no oxygen-delivery identity. (docs/physlib-overlap.md)
findings.confidence: high for the grep; Mathlib and physlib were not searched for heat laws

findings.claim: The lead's profile page does not mention fire or coatings; it describes bio-fabricated material systems and bio-based architecture.
findings.evidence_quote: bio-fabricated material systems for design; bio-based architecture; architectural bio-composite applications from protein and polysaccharide binders
findings.confidence: high (the fire-coating link rests on Amit's brief, not on the page)

key_claims: Elimination certificates on 1-D conduction, char resistance, lumped transient, ignition time and fuel-load energy are provable in Lean/Mathlib today with explicit hypotheses and no new axioms.
They can only reject candidates that break a limit even in their best case inside a stated envelope; they cannot approve any.
The saving in fire tests is bounded by how many candidates fail one thermal criterion; unknown until measured material data exist.
The hypotheses (envelopes, lumped time constant, burn window) carry the real risk; a wrong envelope makes a certificate wrong.

table.name: steady series resistance and back-face rise
table.fields: d, k, Rs, Ra, DT; backRise = DT*Ra/(d/k+Rs+Ra)
table.source: Wikipedia Thermal resistance; Quintiere 2006 and Drysdale 2011 (cited, not opened); NEW to registry

table.name: thermal penetration depth, thick or thin
table.fields: c, alpha, t, d; pdepth = c*sqrt(alpha t)
table.source: SFPE guide (snippet) and textbooks; NEW (nearest registry item: diffusiveTime h^2/D)

table.name: lumped first-order transient
table.fields: Tss, tau, t; relax = Tss(1-exp(-t/tau)), solves tau T' = Tss - T

table.name: thin solid ignition with loss, critical flux
table.fields: T0, Tig, q, h, C=rho c d; q_cr = h(Tig-T0)

table.name: thick and thin ignition time
table.fields: I=k rho c, DTig, q; t=(pi/4) I DTig^2/q^2 ; t=C DTig/q
table.source: SFPE guide; Mikkola and Wichman 1989; Spearpoint and Quintiere 2001; NEW

table.name: energy-balance bound on peak HRR
table.fields: n, dt, E, chi, m, dH

recommendations: Use the certificate only as a pre-screen, after measuring k, density, c and char conductivity of each candidate on small bench samples; those inputs make the envelopes honest.
Pick one concrete regulation criterion, fetch its text, and restate the limit and fire-side temperature curve; I fetched no regulation, so 400 K and 800 K in the worked example are placeholders.
Prove a PDE-level comparison theorem for a layered slab so the lumped time-constant hypothesis can go; not done here.
Make each elimination print its hypotheses so a lab can falsify the envelope cheaply.
Never present survivors as compliant; budget real tests for all of them.

glossary.certificate: a proved theorem: under stated hypotheses a candidate must break a stated limit
glossary.thermally_thick: front-face heating pulse has not reached the back face
glossary.char: insulating carbonised layer formed on heating, modelled as extra resistance
glossary.critical_heat_flux: flux below which a solid never reaches ignition temperature
glossary.lumped_model: one-temperature model with a single time constant tau
glossary.envelope: declared bounds on thickness, conductivity and so on under which a certificate holds
